document.title: Deputy Secretary Armitage-Mamoud Phone Call – September 18, 2001 (State 161279)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), New Documents Detail America's Strategic Response to 9/11
document.note: [Confidential] ISI Director Mahmoud Ahmed travels to Afghanistan on September 17 to meet Mullah Omar and conveys three U.S. conditions: hand over UBL, hand over 13 top lieutenants, and close terrorist training camps. Mahmoud says the Taliban's response was 'not negative on all these points.'

persons.name: Mahmoud Ahmed
persons.role: Director of Pakistan's ISI, Lieutenant General

mentions.quote: PAKISTAN ISI DIRECTOR LIEUTENANT GENERAL MAMOUD AND THE DEPUTY SECRETARY SPOKE BY TELEPHONE FOR 5 MINUTES ON 18 SEPTEMBER
HE HAD THE OPPORTUNITY TO MEET WITH ISLAMIC LEADER MULLAH OMAR
HE ALSO ADDED A FOURTH CONDITION ON HIS OWN
CLASSIFIED BY RICHARD L. ARMITAGE, DEPUTY SECRETARY OF STATE
DEPUTY SECRETARY ARMITAGE THANKED THE GENERAL FOR ADDING THIS FOURTH CONDITION
MEET WITH ISLAMIC LEADER MULLAH OMAR, AS WELL AS OTHER GOVERNMENT AND JUDICIARY MINISTRY OFFICIALS
HE FRAMED THE DECISION TO MULLAH OMAR AND THE OTHER AFGHANS

events.description: Armitage and Mamoud spoke by phone for 5 minutes at 1120
Mamoud traveled to Afghanistan and met Mullah Omar and ministry officials, conveying US demands
Armitage and Mamoud discussed demands in Washington the previous week
Grand Council of Elders expected to meet the next day
Armitage and ISI Director Mahmoud held a 5-minute phone call at 1120 about Mahmoud's Afghanistan trip.
Mahmoud met Mullah Omar and Afghan officials, conveying US demands.
Armitage and Mahmoud discussed demands, expectations and consequences in Washington the week before.
Mahmoud presented conditions: hand over UBL, hand over 13 lieutenants, close terrorist camps, plus a fourth condition of inspections of training sites.
Grand Council of Elders was expected to meet the following day to decide on the demands.
Mahmoud and his wife returned to Pakistan on a US government aircraft.

key_claims: ISI chief Mamoud told the Taliban they must hand over UBL to an international court or extradite him.
Mamoud demanded handover of 13 top UBL lieutenants/associates, some already indicted.
Taliban were required to close all terrorist training camps.
Mamoud added on his own a fourth condition: inspection of training sites by neutral Western observers.
Mamoud said the Afghan response was 'not negative on all these points' and a Grand Council of Elders would decide.
Mamoud framed the choice as UBL and his safe haven versus the welfare of 25 million Afghans.
The US government provided aircraft for Mamoud's and his wife's return to Pakistan.
